processes.name: Complete initialization
processes.summary: A SUB-PROCESS of initialize-harness, called after a harness is installed and also when the location turns out to be an instance of the chosen harness already.

processes.name: Determine the harness and repositories
processes.summary: A SUB-PROCESS of initialize-harness, never an entry point.

processes.name: Human–agent discussion
processes.summary: A REUSABLE SUB-PROCESS, never an entry point.

processes.name: Initialize a harness
processes.summary: THE ONLY PROCESS IN BOOTSTRAP AN ACTOR STARTS.

processes.name: Log a message
processes.summary: A SUB-PROCESS, never an entry point.

processes.name: Render a Knowledge Graph to GitHub Pages
processes.summary: Render a Knowledge Graph — the whole of it, or a list of its Subgraphs — to GitHub Pages at a publication root URL, and report the push: a STATUS (pushed, not pushed, could not determine) and one MESSAGE carrying the deployed commit and the QA result.

processes.name: DIIG — from a health system bottleneck to a costed implementation plan
processes.summary: The nine-chapter sequence of the WHO/ITU Digital Implementation Investment Guide, as the Guide numbers it.

processes.name: Getting started
processes.summary: Somebody said "create a folio": work out which request they meant, with the branch computed by a decision table that may answer "ask", and what has to be true before anything is written.

processes.name: Is the incremental IG AST what a full build would have produced?
processes.summary: The review step of an incremental FHIR IG build, as its own subprocess: list and inspect the differences between the incremental IG AST and what a full build would have produced, then accept them or raise a finding.

processes.name: Narrative review
processes.summary: Judging changed PROSE: read what the mechanical checkers flagged, decide which findings are real, then look at the two things no checker can judge — whether the editorial dependencies still hold and whether a translation still says what the source does.

processes.name: Review task
processes.summary: The generic review position: classify what changed, descend into the review that fits it, consolidate what comes back, and accept or send back.

processes.name: Voice overlay review
processes.summary: The voice axis: load whichever editorial voices are active, run each rule's mechanical half, and decide — for each finding — whether the prose is wrong, the rule does not apply to this content, or this block is a stated exception.

processes.name: Incremental IG build
processes.summary: A proposed incremental build for a WHO SMART Implementation Guide: compile, validate and re-render only the dependency cone of a change, then gate on QA and deploy.

processes.name: L3 FHIR IG pipeline
processes.summary: How a WHO SMART Guidelines L3 FHIR Implementation Guide is modelled, built with SUSHI, the validator and the IG Publisher, reviewed and published.

processes.name: Authoring a document
processes.summary: How a document folio — structured prose and policy guidance, with no Lean and no required TeX — is authored, built and reviewed end to end.

processes.name: Content Change and Review
processes.summary: Getting a change to a folio's CONTENT from a request into a published rendering: the author says what they want, an agent works out its scope and makes it, a review committee accepts or refuses it, and the pipeline deploys.

processes.name: Content lifecycle
processes.summary: One cycle of a folio from plan to retirement, calling editing and the draft-to-publication path as call activities.

processes.name: Draft, review and publish
processes.summary: How the corpus becomes an officially published folio: a draft publication, its review, and the release authority's decision.

processes.name: Editing and HCI validation
processes.summary: What happens to one proposed change to one content block: drafted, validated mechanically and by review, shown to the editor, and committed to the corpus only if accepted.

processes.name: Evidence for a recommendation
processes.summary: Frame a question for a recommendation, retrieve and appraise evidence from trusted sources, and either attach it or record the gap.

processes.name: Is AtomicMass.lean still in sync with its data table?
processes.summary: Check that `AtomicMass.lean` is still in sync with the data table it is generated from.

processes.name: Authoring a paper
processes.summary: How a scientific paper or book folio is authored end to end, with Lean for its formal claims and LaTeX for its typesetting.

processes.name: L2 DAK authoring
processes.summary: How a WHO SMART Guidelines L2 Digital Adaptation Kit is authored by a business analyst, a terminologist and a clinical SME under a programme manager.

processes.name: A sub-graph wants to leave
processes.summary: Part of a repository wants to leave, for size or a semantic reason: four gated stages measure it out of the graph before anything moves, and an administrator authorises the extraction.

processes.name: A knowledge graph leaves for its own repositories
processes.summary: THE METHOD FOR A KNOWLEDGE GRAPH THAT LEAVES FOR ITS OWN REPOSITORIES, AND IT IS TWO REPOSITORIES, NOT ONE.

processes.name: KG to public portal
processes.summary: How a knowledge graph reaches a public portal this repository does not run: select, serialize, package, sign, distribute, and verify on the portal's side.

processes.name: Code node review
processes.summary: Judging changed CODE NODES — Tool definitions and schema definition nodes — on whether they are correct NODES, not merely correct code.

processes.name: Content acquisition
processes.summary: How a resource gets into the graph in the first place.

processes.name: Copy out materialized content — to work on somebody else's bytes
processes.summary: Somebody wants to change content this repository holds a read-only materialized copy of: copy it into their own `folio/`, recording which original it came out of.

processes.name: Document ingestion — uploads/ to the L1 source knowledge graph
processes.summary: The whole path from a file landing in `uploads/` to a citeable L1 source knowledge graph, calling the ingestion subprocesses in turn.

processes.name: Human Translation Workflow
processes.summary: The human half of translation: a coordinator assigns a locale to a qualified translator, the translator works in their own tool, a subject-matter expert judges accuracy, and only then is the result official.

processes.name: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
processes.summary: Build the L1 knowledge graph from what ingestion derived: Dublin Core, the manifest, the assets, their binding and their links.

processes.name: Ingestion subprocess — derive content from the assets
processes.summary: Derive content from an ingested source's assets: the archive, technical metadata, images, audio, tabular data and provenance.

processes.name: Ingestion subprocess — extract structure
processes.summary: Extract the structure of an uploaded source: its text layer, OCR where it has none, sections, structure and claim candidates.

processes.name: Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate
processes.summary: Decide whether the derived content is complete enough to promote to the L1 graph, and who says so.

processes.name: Materialize remote content — the shared subprocess
processes.summary: One process, called wherever remote content is landed locally.

processes.name: Adopt a methodology from a source document
processes.summary: Adopt the method of a shared paper, book or standard: origin and licence, ingestion, what is adopted and refused, placement by ownership, integration by calling existing processes, and the owner's review.

processes.name: Refresh materialized remote content
processes.summary: Keep a materialized copy of remote content current: what changed upstream, what changed locally, and what to do when both did — an archival copy is never re-fetched and gets a fixity check instead.

processes.name: Sample import into a structured data store
processes.summary: The SDLC for testing an import of a SAMPLE of a remote source into a knowledge graph or other structured store.

processes.name: Subscribe to an external knowledge graph
processes.summary: Subscribe a folio or harness to an external knowledge graph pinned to a full commit SHA, then take each chosen part from referenced to materialized through `materialize-remote` and instantiate each chosen harness once its needs are held.

processes.name: Translation Workflow
processes.summary: The machine half of translation, end to end: extract the translatable strings, inject a catalogue back, check the result by back-translating it, and track whether the source has moved since.

processes.name: Deep document research
processes.summary: Answer a question from a corpus this folio ALREADY HOLDS, iteratively, stopping on a stated condition.

processes.name: Actor and role administration
processes.summary: Changing who can do what: adding an actor, opening or closing a role to one, granting or revoking a permission — and auditing the graph afterwards, because the declaration and the graph are two things that can disagree.

processes.name: CRDM close-out
processes.summary: The stakeholders sign off, the BA confirms every criterion is met, and only then does the agent close the issue.

processes.name: CRDM data model
processes.summary: Draft the data model from the BPA and the requirements, have the BA confirm the entities and the stakeholders confirm the cardinalities, and loop until both.

processes.name: CRDM Phase 6 — implement, MVP, acceptance
processes.summary: One phase and not three, because the loops say so: an increment the BA rejects, an MVP that is not ready, and stakeholder findings all route back into implementation.

processes.name: CRDM — link the work to an issue
processes.summary: Scan for a GitHub issue matching the feature work, then link it or ask — an issue is never created without the BA's permission.

processes.name: CRDM Phase 1 — needs
processes.summary: Identify the stakeholders, synthesise a needs statement from the sources, and loop until the BA and the stakeholders both recognise it.

processes.name: CRDM Phases 2–4 — BPA and requirements
processes.summary: Map the current workflow, then define the requirements and the impact they carry, and loop until approved.

processes.name: CRDM requirements
processes.summary: A feature request turned into agreed, signed-off requirements and delivered, with one call activity per CRDM phase from issue linking to close-out.

processes.name: CRDM Phase 5 — beans and sign-off
processes.summary: The approved requirements become work-plan items, the BA signs off, and the branch is announced on the issue.

processes.name: Render a Knowledge Graph to a CDN
processes.summary: Render a Knowledge Graph — the whole of it, or a list of its Subgraphs — for publication to a CDN at a publication root URL, and report a STATUS and a MESSAGE.

processes.name: Session state machine
processes.summary: The shape of a session from the outside: establish who is acting, open a record for them, take each turn in, and write down only what actually changed.

processes.name: SWOT situation analysis
processes.summary: Situation analysis over two axes — internal/external and helpful/harmful — producing the raw material a decision is made from, and NEVER the decision.

processes.name: Agent activity log
processes.summary: What an agent writes down about its own run, and what a person can do with it afterwards: task starts and ends, messages and errors, persisted where somebody can read them.

processes.name: Adjudication
processes.summary: A criterion's reviewer entries disagree and no mechanism can settle them: this is the judgement that does, and the record it must leave.

processes.name: Agent bean lifecycle
processes.summary: The whole life of a work-plan item, and the rules that make one agent's bean legible to another: check before you create, claim before you work, keep the body current as you go, and end it in a state that says why.

processes.name: Is CI actually working on the default branch?
processes.summary: Is CI actually working on the default branch: record each workflow's state on one tracking issue, and fail the job only when the state could not be determined.

processes.name: Code change and review
processes.summary: Getting a change to the PLATFORM from "this is needed" to merged: claim the work, branch and announce it, make the change, prove it against the platform's own gates, and carry it through review to a merge somebody else is not left holding.

processes.name: The gates a change must pass before it can merge
processes.summary: The gates a change must pass before it can merge: the jobs of the code-quality workflow, each marked hard, warn-only or not a gate, joined by one question — did every hard one pass.

processes.name: Criterion adjudication
processes.summary: Two reviewer entries for ONE QA criterion disagree: ask the adjudication, then do the one of three things that a criterion disagreement admits.

processes.name: Publishing the docs site, and keeping the previews alive
processes.summary: Publish the docs site to `gh-pages`, verify the export before the deploy, and keep the open pull requests' previews alive across a deploy that replaces the whole branch.

processes.name: Staging a feature branch preview, and taking it down
processes.summary: The lifecycle of a feature branch's review preview: staged on a push, taken down when its pull request closes, or removed by an explicit dispatch.

processes.name: Are the .jsonld siblings still in sync with their .ts manifests?
processes.summary: Check that the committed `.jsonld` siblings are still in sync with the `.ts` manifests they are generated from.

processes.name: Merge the base branch in
processes.summary: Bring the base branch into a pull-request branch: merge, classify every conflicted path before resolving any, refuse the whole merge if one is authored or undeclared, otherwise resolve, regenerate and prove the result with the gate set.

processes.name: A merge train
processes.summary: Land the ready pull requests as one train: place each by the merge-priority decision table, merge the members with `merge-base`, run the gate set on the combination, and on red eject the culprit rather than reject the train.

processes.name: Prose and the code it describes
processes.summary: Judging whether the prose side of a declared prose/code pair still says what the code does, once the machine has done what it can.

processes.name: Options analysis
processes.summary: A decision reached by a NAMED methodology, with its rejected options recorded.

processes.name: Which open pull requests have no CI run on their head?
processes.summary: Find the open pull requests whose head has no CI run, past an age gate, and say so on one tracking issue and once per head on the pull request.

processes.name: Alert the publication manager
processes.summary: One alert for every failure after the publish button — an incomplete export, a failed verification, a failed deploy, a lost preview — kept as a single tracking issue for the publication manager and closed by the next clean publish.

processes.name: Verify the export before it is deployed
processes.summary: Run the verifier set over the built tree between the export and the deploy, blocking it: pass, fail or could-not-tell, and the caller deploys only on a pass.

processes.name: QA report signing
processes.summary: Attesting a QA report: build the test run, work out what the performer can actually reach, and sign — over the API where that is available, or as release authority where it is not.

processes.name: Related work: find, sort, summarize, ask to coordinate
processes.summary: Before new work takes shape, find the work it touches.

processes.name: Is the repository itself healthy?
processes.summary: Is the repository itself healthy — what the review previews cost the publish branch, what a clone costs, whether the work plan holds duplicates or unhonoured claims — reported in one tracking issue and never acted on.

processes.name: Stalled-agent triage: collect handovers, consolidate themes, recommend, re-route
processes.summary: When agents stall (context exhausted, container lost, session timed out) their work is spread over PRs, branches, beans and process runs.

processes.name: Watching a pinned upstream dependency
processes.summary: Has a pinned upstream dependency fallen behind a release: check each pin, keep one tracking issue, and enter the adoption subprocess for each dependency that is behind.

processes.name: Adopting an upstream version bump
processes.summary: A REUSABLE SUBPROCESS, entered once per pinned upstream dependency that has fallen behind a release.

processes.name: Ingestion subprocess — ingest a theme
processes.summary: Decide whether an ingested artefact is a theme source and, when it is, extract its palette roles and layouts and send them to theme and UI review.

processes.name: Render log — the publish branch keeps its own history
processes.summary: Every change to the publish branch appends an entry to `_render-log/<day>.jsonl`.

processes.name: Theme and UI review — at ingestion
processes.summary: Reviewing GRAPHICAL ASSETS AS THEY ARE INGESTED — accessibility, branding, languages — in the context of the website or app design they are for, to determine what the graphical assets and the UI are going to be.

processes.name: Wireframe design review
processes.summary: WireGen (methodologies/wiregen) made executable: a written design intent, at least two mid-fidelity candidates each with a web AND a mobile layout, mechanical checks, a blind per-criterion review, adjudication where reviewers disagree, and a recorded choice.

processes.name: Board: open and close content
processes.summary: What a reader does to a board and what the renderer does back: every card rests as its avatar, a window opens onto the one the reader chose, and it closes back to where it came from.

processes.name: Board: place a note
processes.summary: Putting a note at a spot on a board: write the note into the folio, record where it was drawn on THIS board, and sweep any position whose note has gone.

processes.name: Board: relocate content to the trashcan
processes.summary: Moving open content to the trashcan from the board, with the reader's confirmation in front of the move and not behind it.
